# pbs_notification_test (Action)

Has a Proxmox Backup Server send a test notification through a notification endpoint — sendmail, SMTP, Gotify or webhook —, as **Test** in the Notifications panel does, and fails when PBS cannot deliver it. PBS answers once it has tried: an SMTP server gets 5 seconds, a Gotify server or webhook 10; for a sendmail endpoint, success means that the node's mail system took the message, not that it arrived.

The notification has the subject "Test notification", severity `info` and no metadata fields, and goes to the endpoint directly: the notification matchers play no part, so the test says nothing about which notifications they route to the endpoint, and PBS has no call to test a matcher. A disabled endpoint is tested all the same; the action then warns, as PBS sends it nothing else. PBS ignores a Gotify, SMTP or webhook endpoint whose secrets are missing from its configuration, and answers that it does not exist.

The endpoint resources test an endpoint whenever they create or change it with `send_test_on_apply`; the action tests one whenever it runs, such as after a change of something the delivery depends on — `http_proxy` of `pbs_node_config` for Gotify and webhooks —, or with `terraform apply -invoke`.

Needs `Sys.Modify on /system/notifications`.

-> Actions need Terraform 1.14.1 or later. OpenTofu and older Terraform releases do not support them, and Terraform 1.13 ignores `action` blocks without a word; set `required_version = ">= 1.14.1"` in configurations that use them. An action runs when a resource's `lifecycle` `action_trigger` fires, or with `terraform apply -invoke=action.<type>.<name>`, which also refreshes the state of the resources the action's configuration refers to, and of those they depend on, but of no other resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  # Actions need Terraform 1.14.1 or later; Terraform 1.13 would ignore them.
  required_version = ">= 1.14.1"
}

resource "pbs_node_config" "this" {
  http_proxy = "http://proxy.example.com:3128"

  # Gotify notifications go through the node's proxy: check that they still
  # arrive whenever the node's settings change.
  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_update]
      actions = [action.pbs_notification_test.phone]
    }
  }
}

resource "pbs_notification_endpoint_gotify" "phone" {
  name             = "phone"
  server           = "https://gotify.example.com"
  token_wo         = var.gotify_token
  token_wo_version = 1
}

# Or send a test notification yourself:
# terraform apply -invoke=action.pbs_notification_test.phone
action "pbs_notification_test" "phone" {
  config {
    name = pbs_notification_endpoint_gotify.phone.name
  }
}

variable "gotify_token" {
  description = "Token of the Gotify application PBS sends to."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  ephemeral   = true
}
```

<!-- action schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the endpoint, such as `pbs_notification_endpoint_smtp.mail.name`, or `mail-to-root`, the sendmail endpoint PBS ships.
